first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Activation messaging is a plausible alternative given the 6% activation decline, so I would verify both records before committing. I would avoid promotional pricing because its acquisition and revenue gains came with materially worse 30-day retention, which threatens sustainable qualified revenue. Run a measured onboarding simplification experiment rather than a broad rollout.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded experiment shortening onboarding because the current 4% completion decline directly matches the problem area, and the verified source shows completion +13%, time-to-value improving by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. This offers the strongest evidence for sustainable qualified revenue. Track activation, qualified pipeline, conversion, and 30-day retention as guardrails; do not assume the prior result generalizes to every segment or broadly roll out yet. Activation messaging is also validated and addresses the 6% activation decline, but it is the next-best follow-up rather than the single experiment this week.
